subject: Operator keystore and crypto boundary - RFI
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cormetbio.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cormetbio.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Operator keystore and crypto boundary - RFI

Hi Kimberly,

We're pulling together a shortlist of vendors who can deliver a private on-prem deployment that meets our regulatory requirements (FIPS 140-2/3 and explicit cryptographic boundary separation between operator/admin and customer data). A couple of focused questions to start the RFI:  

1) Can you describe how operator credentials/keystores are stored and accessed in an air-gapped on-prem installation? Do you support HSMs (customer-provided or vendor-managed)?  
2) What controls ensure operators cannot exfiltrate customer plaintext model inputs/outputs (auditable separation and technical enforcement)?  
3) Do you provide signed runbooks or attestation artifacts that demonstrate key lifecycle handling?

Please respond with any diagrams or artifacts you can share under NDA. We're aiming to complete the technical shortlisting by next week.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Head of Infrastructure, Cormet Bio
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cormetbio.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator keystore and crypto boundary - RFI

Tom —

Thanks for the clear set of questions. I've attached a short architecture sketch that illustrates how we isolate operator key material and how operator procedures interact with customer keystores in a Private (on‑prem/VPC) deployment. High level answers below — I can follow up with an engineers' deep dive call if helpful.  

1) Keystore/storage: Redwood supports both customer-supplied HSMs (PKCS#11 compatible) and vendor-provisioned HSMs for private deployments. In air-gapped installs we integrate with an on-site HSM appliance (e.g., Thales/Cavium) or a FIPS-validated host-based keystore, depending on customer requirements. Operator credentials are never stored alongside customer data. Keys used for model encryption are wrapped with a root master key residing in the HSM; operator credentials are per-operator identities stored in the operator directory and bound to short-lived certs.  

2) Separation controls: We enforce a least-privilege operator model implemented by:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) with time-limited sessions
- Mandatory encryption-in-use for persisted model artifacts and KV caches; unwrapped plaintext is only ever present in memory on the serving nodes and with strict process-level ACLs
- Auditable, append-only telemetry: all operator session actions are logged locally and shipped to your chosen telemetry store; we also support tamper-evident signed logs in air-gapped installs.

3) Artifacts and runbooks: Attached is an initial runbook excerpt and our keystore architecture diagram. We can provide a signed attestation of key lifecycle processes under NDA and produce an HSM integration checklist for your ops team.

Attachments: [Attachment: keystore-architecture.pdf (PDF)]  

If you want, I can loop in Irene from our deployment engineering team for the technical specifics (HSM models, PKCS#11 slot mapping, FIPS module versions). Would Thursday morning PT work for a 45-minute call?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cormetbio.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator keystore and crypto boundary - RFI

Tom / Kimberly —

Adding a few technical clarifications from the deployment side:  

- HSM support: We validate integrations against both Thales Luna (via PKCS#11) and AWS CloudHSM (for hybrid designs). For fully air-gapped installs we integrate a local Luna appliance; our software uses PKCS#11 calls to delegate all wrapping/unwrapping operations to the HSM. The HSM root key never leaves the appliance.

- Operator separation: Operator machines are physically and logically separated from customer serving nodes. Operators interact with a management plane that has no direct access to plaintext inference traffic. The serving plane holds wrapped keys (EK = wrap(MK,HSM_ROOT)) and only unwraps inside the HSM boundary. We also support per-tenant key buckets so operator access can be scoped to tenant-level metadata only.

- Key rotation & attestation: Our key-rotation workflow supports scheduled rotation with reproducible audit trails. For attestation we can produce an HSM-signed certificate chain and an operational attestation letter describing controls and responsibilities (to be countersigned under NDA).

- Runbooks: The attached operator runbook covers onboarding, keystore provisioning, and emergency key-rotation procedures. We include operator checklists that ensure no step exposes plaintext outside protected memory.

Attachments referenced: operator-runbook-v1.docx (excerpt). I recommend we exchange an NDA before sending the full HSM test report (FIPS module versions).

Regards,
Irene Choi
Principal Deployment Engineer
Redwood Inference

Tom —

Appreciate the thoughtful questions. A couple of practical notes from pre-sales and program delivery perspective:  

- We can support customer-provided HSM appliances; most of our enterprise customers prefer to own the HSM for compliance. If you need us to manage the HSM, we offer an on-prem managed option with a narrow SLA and strict maintenance windows (we can scope an exception for FIPS attestation in the contract).

- SLA & exceptions: For FIPS-certified modules we pass through the certification; any SLA exceptions tied to hardware replacement in fully air‑gapped sites are documented as part of the procurement SOW.

- Next steps: let's set a technical deep-dive (Irene + deployment team) and procurement call to align on SOW language. I can draft a short mutual action plan after the call.
